topic: Energy Resources: Coal, Petroleum and Renewable (Geography)
description: Energy resources are the backbone of a nation's industrial and economic development. In geography, they are primarily classified into conventional (exhaustible) and non-conventional (renewable) sources of energy.

sections.title: Classification of Energy Resources
sections.description: The primary classification of energy resources based on their availability and long-term sustainability.

key_concepts.explanation: These are traditional sources of energy that have been used for a long time and are exhaustible (non-renewable) in nature. Examples include coal, petroleum, natural gas, and firewood.
These are renewable sources of energy that are eco-friendly and inexhaustible. Examples include solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, and biogas.

important_facts.fact: Currently, India relies heavily on thermal power (predominantly coal) to meet the majority of its electricity requirements.
India is the third-largest consumer of primary energy in the world, following China and the United States.

sections.title: Coal: India's Major Energy Source
sections.description: The types of coal, its geographical distribution, and major coal mining regions in India.

key_concepts.explanation: Based on carbon content, coal is classified into four types: Anthracite (80-95% carbon, best quality), Bituminous (60-80% carbon, most widely used in India), Lignite (40-55% carbon, brown coal), and Peat (<40% carbon, lowest grade).

geographical_data.location_or_origin: River valleys of Damodar, Mahanadi, Godavari, and Wardha (primarily in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh).
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Accounts for about 98% of India's total coal reserves. It is mainly high-grade bituminous coal that is approximately 250 million years old.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: North-Eastern states like Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Arunachal Pradesh.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: Much younger than Gondwana coal (15-60 million years old), primarily containing lignite and sub-bituminous coal. Neyveli in Tamil Nadu holds the largest lignite reserves.

important_facts.fact: Jharia (Jharkhand) is the largest and one of the oldest coalfields in India.
Raniganj (West Bengal) is considered the birthplace of coal mining in India, where commercial extraction began in 1774.

sections.title: Petroleum and Natural Gas
sections.description: The extraction and distribution of petroleum (often called liquid gold) and natural gas in India.

key_concepts.explanation: Petroleum (mineral oil) and natural gas are invariably found trapped within the pores and layers of sedimentary rocks, formed by the decomposition of organic matter over millions of years.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: An offshore oilfield located 176 km off the coast of Mumbai in the Arabian Sea.
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is India's largest oil-producing region, contributing to more than 50% of the country's total crude oil production.
Digboi is the oldest oil field in India. Assam holds the distinction of being the oldest oil-producing state in the country.
It is one of the most prominent onshore oil and natural gas fields in Western India.

key_associations.extra_info: It is India's first cross-state gas pipeline, supplying vital natural gas to fertilizer and power plants in Western and Northern India.

important_facts.fact: The Jamnagar Refinery in Gujarat, operated by Reliance Industries, is the largest oil refinery in the world.

sections.title: Renewable Energy: Solar and Wind
sections.description: The future of energy generation focusing on clean, limitless, and environmentally friendly sources.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The direct conversion of light energy into electrical energy.
scientific_principles.application: Solar panels utilize semiconductors like silicon to absorb sunlight and generate an electric current via the photovoltaic effect.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest solar power park in the world by capacity (2245 MW).
It is the largest onshore wind farm in India and one of the largest in the world.

important_facts.fact: The headquarters of the International Solar Alliance (ISA), a global initiative spearheaded by India, is located in Gurugram, Haryana.
At the COP26 summit (2021), India announced its 'Panchamrit' strategy, which includes the ambitious target of achieving 'net-zero' carbon emissions by the year 2070.

sections.title: Nuclear and Hydroelectric Energy
sections.description: Energy generated by harnessing radioactive elements and the kinetic energy of flowing water.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter nuclei, accompanied by the release of a massive amount of energy.
scientific_principles.application: Nuclear Power Plants use Uranium-235 or Plutonium-239 to initiate a controlled chain reaction inside a nuclear reactor to produce electricity.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Established in 1969 with the assistance of the USA, it is India's first commercial nuclear power station.
Built in collaboration with Russia, it is the highest-capacity nuclear power plant in India.

key_associations.extra_info: The beach sands of the Malabar coast in Kerala contain some of the world's largest reserves of Thorium, which is highly strategic for India's future nuclear energy program.
It is the largest multipurpose river valley hydroelectric project in North India. Its reservoir is known as Gobind Sagar.

important_facts.fact: India's first-ever hydroelectric power plant was established in 1897 at Sidrapong in Darjeeling, West Bengal.
